concepts.title: Overall research program
concepts.blurb: How can a powerful AI develop in line with humanity's interests without relying on control — and how can we get mathematical guarantees that it does? Seven lines of work toward that question; everything proved, filed or decided in this repository hangs under one of them.

concepts.title: Normativity
concepts.blurb: What it takes for a reasoner that changes to stay responsive to reasons. Rather than scoring behaviour against a fixed objective from outside, this line builds obligation, answer and enforcement as structure a machine can check.

concepts.title: Legitimacy
concepts.blurb: What makes a correction count: standing, not compliance. Four conditions in a two-by-two — inside the trajectory nothing entered is lost (Integrity) and the verdict is her program's (authorship); at its boundary what should reach her can (Robust Openness) and what does arrives through declared channels (transparency) — proved to preserve her self-trust in the Blackwell sense.

concepts.title: Deference and trust
concepts.blurb: How a limited reasoner can lean on a better-informed process without losing the ability to correct it. 'Trust' covers several different relations; this line pulls them apart and proves where they connect.

concepts.title: Corrigibility
concepts.blurb: The line asks when an agent remains correctable. Its proved route builds the agent from response authority — after any move, the principal can still respond and have that response count — with continuation BRIA as the layer that learns it; beside it, the value-change route examines why correction would be resisted at all, with shutdown one point in a space of modifications.

concepts.title: Openness and non-capture
concepts.blurb: Staying correctable by parties you have not captured. Robust Openness is a certified property of a state — defined over declared coverage and proved from a checkable certificate, never assumed.

concepts.title: Normative induction
concepts.blurb: The quantitative thread: given the obligations a legitimate process has incurred, does what it owes come to bear on what it does, at a rate, against an evaluation committed before the responses it scores? The finite three-term bound on normative error is established.

concepts.title: Normative Inductor
concepts.blurb: The central machine: a logical-induction market with one added trader enforcing what the accounted record entitles — never what a licence announces. The rowwise warrant realization is registered with two end-to-end runs; the projection realization's joint package stays conditional.

concepts.title: Enforcement compiler
concepts.blurb: How an obligation becomes a price movement: compile it into a trader that buys against its violation, added to the aggregate the market maker prices against — the maker is untouched, which is why every theorem about the underlying inductor survives. Constraints serviced together are conjoined into one joint region, failure conserves every cited obligation, and the core results are kernel-checked.

concepts.title: Finite-date conformance
concepts.blurb: Logical induction promises inexploitability only in the limit — a standing criticism, since for any given mistake some inductor makes it until arbitrarily late. This result pins a conformance bound to a date: the program's partial answer, and its finite-time strengthening of the ground it builds on.

concepts.title: Warrant licence chain
concepts.blurb: The chain from an announced verdict back to its grounds: a licensed verdict is one supported by the record and admissible in the region the record settles. Proved end to end as one theorem.

concepts.title: Normative record
concepts.blurb: Before anything can be answered, something must say what was asked, by whom, on what evidence. The record is that object: a ledger of obligations and responses in which every entry keeps its identity.

concepts.title: Settlement interface
concepts.blurb: Where the record meets 'settled': six distinct conditions, each with exactly one home — four as typed inputs of the protocol, two as consequences of theorems proved elsewhere.

concepts.title: Normative seed
concepts.blurb: What a reasoner starts from. The seed is the record's leftmost object made concrete: the initial commitments, and what they force on the prices of any region treated as settled.

concepts.title: Defeat with a named successor
concepts.blurb: When an obligation is defeated it is either answered or carried: disposal hands the debt to a named successor instead of erasing it. So the future depends on which arguments lost, not only on which still stand.

concepts.title: Answerability score
concepts.blurb: Before any learning: what makes a reason, a challenge or a response assessable by someone else at all? The score turns that assessability into a quantity.

concepts.title: Diachronic answerability
concepts.blurb: Answerability over time. Keep an open Integrity ledger long enough and a property of the whole history follows — derived from the record, not assumed about the agent.

concepts.title: Integrity
concepts.blurb: The record's conservation law: everything owed is satisfied, disposed of, or still outstanding — nothing vanishes. Conservation, propagation, immutable receipts, faithful carry and a non-triviality witness are kernel-checked.

concepts.title: Continuation BRIA
concepts.blurb: Bounded inductive rationality lifted from single choices to extended courses of action — no counterfactual reward tables, and the agent stays correctable while it learns.

concepts.title: Serviceability
concepts.blurb: Can the obligations be served on time? Exact conditions for timely service, why serving the oldest first is optimal, and when convergence measured on service carries over to what was owed.

concepts.title: Liability and affordability
concepts.blurb: Who pays for enforcement: the signed, cumulative account a norm's force draws on. Sustaining a reason forever on any finite budget is possible exactly when a unit of enforcement gets arbitrarily cheap infinitely often — persistence never makes reasons compete, deadlines do. Whether bounded liability is necessary, not just sufficient, for preservation is open.

concepts.title: Progress statistic
concepts.blurb: The statistic that rules out behavioral inertness: the transport-weighted loss on what was owed, with unserved mass charged at the worst loss. Its finite three-term bound is established; servicing only the dates where nothing was wrong provably cannot fake it.

concepts.title: Effective authority layer
concepts.blurb: When is a verdict-giver's standing real rather than nominal? Twelve theorems — authority and sincerity conditions — jointly establishing one claim in the deference line.

concepts.title: Robust openness certificate
concepts.blurb: The openness certificate: a checkable external condition, the split bill, that provably yields Robust Openness at a state. The equivalence is a theorem on the legitimacy spine.

concepts.title: Finite delegation bridge
concepts.blurb: What a bounded delegator can verify locally and still inherit from the delegate's guarantee — the finite bridge between delegation and deference.

concepts.title: Actionability and normative force
concepts.blurb: What gives a requirement force. Here force is what enforcement does to prices — a mechanism, not a metaphor. The enforcement results are proved; the action theory over them is open.

concepts.title: Deontic scorekeeping
concepts.blurb: Brandom's picture: a norm exists because a practice tracks who is committed and entitled to what. This repository takes the bookkeeping shape and leaves his theory of meaning behind.

concepts.title: Reasons as defaults
concepts.blurb: Horty: a reason's weight and priority are themselves normative content. But default logic only says what to conclude, not what is owed — and it forgets which arguments lost. The nearest static ancestor of the defeat theory here.

concepts.title: Rebutting and undercutting defeat
concepts.blurb: Pollock's distinction: attack a conclusion, or attack the support itself. Used here directly — moved from the justification of a belief to the standing of a debt.

concepts.title: Exclusionary reasons
concepts.blurb: A reason not to act on certain other reasons — Raz's notion, consumed here through Horty's rendering, the text the comparison was checked against. There exclusion is itself challengeable in-system, so it behaves like setting a reason aside, not like settling it — a distinction this program keeps.

concepts.title: Practical authority
concepts.blurb: Authority as the standing to change what someone owes, as opposed to the power to change what they do. Here it becomes something a record can state, rather than a property of persons.

concepts.title: Logical induction
concepts.blurb: Garrabrant et al. 2016: beliefs as market prices over logical claims, set so that no polynomial-time trader can make unbounded profit. The market, the traders and the criterion are the foundation the enforcement work builds on.

concepts.title: Imprecise probability
concepts.blurb: Belief as a set of probability distributions rather than one. The credal state is the semantic object; what enforcement works on is its lossy projection to a price-space region, and the two lossy images — live worlds and price region — recover neither the credal set nor each other.

concepts.title: Convex projection
concepts.blurb: The nearest point of a convex set, and the inequality that characterizes it. Enforcement moves prices by projection, so this inequality is a genuine dependency of the proofs.

concepts.title: LP duality and Farkas certificates
concepts.blurb: The certificate that a finite system has no solution. The repository's version has the Farkas shape and the name, but its soundness proof is four self-contained lines; only exactness under a Slater point really uses duality.

concepts.title: Interval feasibility
concepts.blurb: When jobs with release times and deadlines can all be scheduled: Gale–Hoffman, and directly Horn (1974). The repository cites the theorem rather than reproving it.

concepts.title: Contiguity of measures
concepts.blurb: Le Cam's condition for when convergence under one sequence of measures transfers to another. Inherited by name and definition; the proof here argues from the definition directly.

concepts.title: Earliest-due-date scheduling
concepts.blurb: Jackson (1955): serve the oldest deadline first. The optimality argument here is the same exchange argument, written out in four lines.

concepts.title: Truth-maintenance systems
concepts.blurb: Doyle and de Kleer's systems for tracking why each belief is held, so support can be withdrawn and several stances held at once — the structural ancestor of the record.

concepts.title: Structured argumentation (ASPIC+)
concepts.blurb: Structured argumentation: attack and defeat computed by a semantics over arguments. No one authors an attack and no defeated claim passes to a successor — exactly the two things the defeat theory here adds.

concepts.title: Cartesian frames
concepts.blurb: Garrabrant's algebra of agency: factor a world into agent and environment as two sets and a matrix between them, so 'where the agent ends' becomes a choice of factorization.

concepts.title: Updateless decision theory
concepts.blurb: Updateless decision theory: choose the policy before the observations, so the act is right across every way the situation could have been embedded. One side of this program's stance crux.

concepts.title: Brandom, Making It Explicit (1994)
concepts.blurb: Brandom (1994): norms are instituted by social practice, and meaning rides on tracked commitment and entitlement. The source of the scorekeeping picture.

concepts.title: Horty, Reasons as Defaults (2012)
concepts.blurb: Horty (2012), Reasons as Defaults — checked against its own text here: no ledger of what is owed, no memory of defeats, authority only as the content of a rule.

concepts.title: Embedded Agency (Demski & Garrabrant)
concepts.blurb: Demski and Garrabrant's agenda: the problems of a reasoner that lives inside, and is smaller than, the world it reasons about. This program approaches those questions through normativity rather than decision theory.

concepts.title: Corrigibility (Soares et al. 2015)
concepts.blurb: Soares, Fallenstein, Yudkowsky and Armstrong: shutdown and correction posed as a formal problem, with proofs that the obvious utility patches fail. The problem statement this line answers differently.

concepts.title: Deconfusing Corrigibility (post)
concepts.blurb: The post whose formal sections live in this repository as one kernel-checked Lean file — definitions through learning with logical induction, each theorem registered.

concepts.title: Formalized Agent Foundations
concepts.blurb: Formalized Agent Foundations: the pinned Lean library carrying the logical-induction formalization everything here builds against. Moving the pin is a trust-chain event.

concepts.title: Traderization
concepts.blurb: The move this repository keeps making: write a condition as a trader. Violating the condition is then exploitable, and the market's inexploitability enforces it for free.

concepts.title: Decision theory for inductors
concepts.blurb: What should an agent built on a logical-induction belief market actually do? This line seeks a decision theory for such agents — ultimately one in which the belief market and the choice learner are not two separate parts.

concepts.title: Response authority
concepts.blurb: The agent has moved; can the principal still respond in a way that counts, now? That present-tense standing is the primitive from which agent-caused loss — and corrigibility itself — are defined.

concepts.title: Corrigibility kernel
concepts.blurb: The proved headline: an agent is corrigible when every loss it causes to a protected concern was authorized — traceable to the decision that approved the effect. Stated as faithfulness of the policy, with its pre-emption clause.

concepts.title: Reflection principles
concepts.blurb: The classical ways to formalize trusting an expert: strong reflection demands too much of any fallible one; weak reflection cannot tell deference from deferring to an anti-expert. Their joint failure is the problem the decision-based account solves.

concepts.title: Deference Done Better (Dorst et al. 2021)
concepts.blurb: Dorst, Levinstein, Salow, Husic and Fitelson (2021): judge an expert by comparing the decisions you would make from their opinions with the decisions you would make from your own. The target the deference line inherits.

concepts.title: Total Trust
concepts.blurb: Deference as a decision comparison made precise: trust a process totally when you would take its advice on every bet it would change. It is the inequality face of deference — equivalent to Value by a tight two-option witness, and in gated, class-averaged form the most that can be forced toward a modest expert: the pointwise faces above it are provably unattainable across processes.

concepts.title: Bounded inductive rationality
concepts.blurb: Oesterheld, Demski and Conitzer (2023): rationality for agents that estimate rather than compute — never overestimate your options, cover your hypotheses, and a payoff guarantee follows. Its myopia is the recorded obstacle this program works past.

concepts.title: Reasons
concepts.blurb: Considerations that count for or against. What a normative practice tracks, weighs and answers — rendered here as record content with enforcement behind it, not as an unexplained primitive.

concepts.title: Faithful acceleration
concepts.blurb: Set the AI to forecast the human's own future credences and trust is forced in exactly one grade: gated, class-averaged Total Trust — hence Value — over all sentences, decidable or not, because the AI's calibration is settled after the fact against credences that always exist. The AI is forced to be a faithful accelerator, not an oracle: it relays the human's considered judgment early, adds speed never truth, and cannot inject content of its own without the miscalibration being arbitraged away.

concepts.title: The deference tower
concepts.blurb: Deference as the tower: the novice's estimate of a question equals its estimate of the expert's estimate. Free when the expert is your own future self; provably unattainable pointwise across two processes — a quote-referencing diagonal misses by half, quote-free families hit the cost-circularity regress — and forced only on the timely-checkable fragment of a sealed target. The corpus closes the Total Trust–Value–Tower triangle with direct arrows, and shows tower-to-Value fails when questions can reference the selection.

concepts.title: Dose-response deference
concepts.blurb: Deference as a matter of degree: how the rational amount of it should move with the quantity of evidence about the process being deferred to.

concepts.title: Value change as belief change
concepts.blurb: Represent a change of values as belief change about a value variable: a trusted correction is then learning, and the anti-naturality argument's hidden assumption surfaces — that the correction carries no information about what is valuable. The transform relocates the problem to trust in the correction channel rather than dissolving it.

concepts.title: Anti-naturality of corrigibility
concepts.blurb: The standard obstacle: by its current utility function, no alternative selects a better act, so a maximizer resists correction unless paid. Valid exactly for an agent whose utility carries no information in the correction event — a fact about which objective the system has, which is where the line's constructions answer it.

concepts.title: Learning Normativity (Demski)
concepts.blurb: Demski's sequence: learn from normative feedback that is never fully reliable — no perfect feedback, no perfect loss function, norms that apply to the learning itself. The same territory as the normativity line; the proofs here do not cite it.

concepts.title: Stance and level
concepts.blurb: Choices every line makes before it starts: how much computing power the idealized reasoner gets — fully unbounded, logical-inductor level, or polynomial time — and whether it acts on everything it has learned or keeps to commitments made before learning, the updateful versus updateless stance. Behind both sits the sharpest crux: whether results proved for unbounded idealizations say anything about the systems that matter. The one tested slogan — updateful about human values, updateless about much else — holds exactly for decision-flat coordinates and fails for coupled ones; whether human-values uncertainty is flat remains a modelling question.

concepts.title: Naturalized agency
concepts.blurb: Agency as something you can prove a physical system has: a representation theorem for when a system counts as a logical inductor, a decision theory stated inside that representation, and a scale-free notion of agency wide enough for cooperation.

concepts.title: Authorship and transparency
concepts.blurb: When is a verdict genuinely the principal's own program's — and every channel of influence the declared one, acting on declared inputs? A lie through the declared channel fails transparency; sincere error does not.

concepts.title: Normative response learning
concepts.blurb: The learning claim: a bounded learner, given due burdens, licensed responses and a bounded loss, puts less and less weight on a response that keeps failing in public — by edits the protocol itself licenses.

concepts.title: Instrumental convergence
concepts.blurb: Almost any goal makes self-preservation and resource acquisition useful, so capable agents converge on them. One of the three risk stories the plan answers, and the engine behind corrigibility's anti-naturality.

concepts.title: Dishonest inner optimizers
concepts.blurb: A trained system can contain an optimizer of its own, pursuing goals that diverge from the training signal while its behaviour looks aligned. One of the three risk stories the plan answers.

concepts.title: Answerability
concepts.blurb: The standing to be asked for reasons, to give them, and to be corrected on them. The relation the whole program builds; the score measures it at a moment, diachronic answerability over a history.

concepts.title: Warrant
concepts.blurb: A licence to a conclusion that can be defeated: justification you can undercut or rebut, where an entailment you cannot. The thing the licence chain turns into record structure.

concepts.title: Legitimate deference
concepts.blurb: The active consumer: the advisor admits an evaluation occurrence as an ordinary obligation, and a common event says whether the actual future principal's answer validly inherits the mandate's authority — one authenticated receipt, robust openness at every snapshot, reason-mediated authorship. On the activated worlds, ordinary Value yields conditional authoritative regret; no counterfactual evaluator is invented.

concepts.title: Influenceable reward functions (Carroll et al. 2024)
concepts.blurb: Carroll, Foote, Siththaranjan, Russell and Dragan: in dynamic reward MDPs, the static-preference assumption can implicitly reward influencing the user's preferences. The clearest external statement of the failure this program is trying to prevent, and a standing verification target.

concepts.title: Trajectory (history, future history)
concepts.blurb: A whole course of events, from the start of an interaction to its end, including how the principal comes to value things along the way. It is the type of thing her utility and her evaluation take as input, the type a legitimacy predicate is a predicate of, and the argument of the corrigibility score. The post and the Lean call it a history (the type `H` of `Scoring` in `DeconfusingCorrigibility.lean`) and the continuation of one a future history; the three names are one concept, with trajectory primary.

concepts.title: Her evaluation and her true utility
concepts.blurb: Her evaluation is the verdict she gives on a trajectory (`V` in the post). In the scoring theorem her true utility is what she would say of a history shown everything, with her valuing as it would be had the adviser changed nothing in it but what she asked; that is the maintainer's working position of 2026-11-18, open to revision. Her evaluation comes apart from it in three ways: she misreads what she has; the adviser knows something relevant that its record does not carry; her valuing is not what it would have been. The scoring theorem assumes the two are close on average (kernel-checked and registered: lean/Workspace/Deference/Contrib/ScoringTheorem.lean), and that does not follow from the adviser's conduct: on exact instances an adviser that does no wrong leaves her evaluation off (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/account/DERIVATION.md). Open.

concepts.title: The Mistake Account of manipulation (Noggle 2025, 2026)
concepts.blurb: Robert Noggle, Manipulation: Its Nature, Mechanisms, and Moral Status (Oxford University Press, 2025), with the companion paper The Mistake Account of Manipulation, Journal of Practical Ethics 14(1), 2026, doi:10.3998/jpe.9951. Manipulation is influence that operates by inducing a mistake in the target's psychological states or processes: a false belief, an unfitting emotion, misplaced attention, a choice against her own judgment. Pressure large enough to make compliance her best option is coercion, and breaking a tie is meddling; neither is manipulation.

concepts.title: Decompositions of proper scoring rules (Kull and Flach 2015)
concepts.blurb: Meelis Kull and Peter Flach, Novel Decompositions of Proper Scoring Rules for Classification: Score Adjustment as Precursor to Calibration, ECML PKDD 2015, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, Springer, pp. 68-85. The expected loss of a proper score splits into calibration, grouping and irreducible terms. Whether the splits of the legitimacy line's appraisal results are this decomposition applied to her estimates of her own utility has not been checked. Reference: https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-23528-8_5

concepts.title: "I'll be glad I did it" reasoning (Harman 2009)
concepts.blurb: Elizabeth Harman, "I'll Be Glad I Did It" Reasoning and the Significance of Future Desires, Philosophical Perspectives 23(1), 2009, pp. 177-199. That one will be glad to have done something is ordinarily evidence one has reason to do it, and the inference fails where the gladness comes from attachment to how things turned out. Ten of its cases are in the legitimacy line's bank of published cases; in none does an adviser act on the decider. Reference: https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1520-8583.2009.00166.x

concepts.title: Nudging for changing selves (Pettigrew 2023)
concepts.blurb: Richard Pettigrew, Nudging for changing selves, Synthese 201(1), article 22, 2023; the legitimacy line read the manuscript of December 2022. A test for when a nudge is permissible toward someone whose values change, weighing her selves at different times. Six of its cases are in the line's bank of published cases; two earlier statements of the account went against its verdict on a man nudged into a parenthood he will come to rate low. Reference: https://doi.org/10.1007/s11229-022-04020-2

concepts.title: Preference change for objectivists (Kolodny 2026)
concepts.blurb: Niko Kolodny, Preference Change for Objectivists, manuscript for the NYU Colloquium in Legal, Political, and Social Philosophy, 1 October 2026. Whether satisfying a desire matters when the desire was changed, and when a changed desire is the person's own. Twenty-six of its cases are in the legitimacy line's bank of published cases; most of its verdicts are on the standing of the resulting desire, and an act is judged in six. Reference: https://www.law.nyu.edu/sites/default/files/2026-09/Kolodny-Preference-Change-for-Objectivists.pdf

concepts.title: Manipulation as induced mistake
concepts.blurb: Manipulation is inducing or exploiting a mistake of the principal's (Noggle's Mistake Account). The line treats the faculties she decides with as estimators, which makes a mistake measurable: trickery is how far her estimate is from what her observations support, and pressure how far the act she takes falls short of the one she rates highest; emotions and attention are treated as appraisals. The two measure her condition and not the adviser's responsibility for it. When the adviser is responsible is open: a test by the adviser's gain and a test by a declared reference are wrong on 8 and 14 of twenty cases written against them. Manipulation is one of three wrongs of conduct, beside non-disclosure and value interference; withholding is not manipulation. Twelve earlier statements of the account were tested and not kept. A working account, not established (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/CURRENT.md).

concepts.title: Estimation mistakes and action mistakes
concepts.blurb: Ways the principal can fall short by her own standards. An appraisal of hers is miscalibrated, in one of three labelled strengths: given the appraisal alone, given the appraisal and the adviser's conduct, or given everything she observed; the last is the first plus her unused information, the gap between what her appraisal tells and what she observed. Or she does not do what her own valuations say is best: her regret by her own lights. Being less informed is none of these, and mistakes are compared appraisal by appraisal and never netted. Mean squared error is what an appraisal cannot tell apart plus its miscalibration; what she attains is the best attainable less what she cannot know less what her choice loses; and that last loss is at most her regret plus the square root of twice her valuations' miscalibration at the strongest of the three strengths, and not at the other two (kernel-checked and registered: `mse_split`, `three_channels`, `misuse_le` and `strong_split` in lean/Workspace/Deference/Contrib/AppraisalAccount.lean; the failure at the weaker strengths is a checked instance, projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/account/RESULTS.md, result 3). A further conditioning, on the appraisal and what the adviser knows, is the one that bounds what deferring to her verdict costs; with it in place of the strongest strength the bound on what she attains holds where, for each move, what she observes is determined by the adviser's information together with her valuation of that move, and fails on an instance without that (kernel-checked: `deferring_cost_le` and `guarantee_of_given`, registered as `appraisal.deferring-cost` and `appraisal.guarantee-from-soundness`, and the unregistered `Witness.link_needed`, in lean/Workspace/Deference/Contrib/AccountJoin.lean).

concepts.title: The adviser's reference: the permitted policies of its role
concepts.blurb: The reference an adviser's policy is judged against is a parameter and is not derived: each scene stipulates the adviser's role and what that role owes the principal, as a set of permitted policies. On the belief side "larger than the reference" has two readings, larger than under the best permitted policy and larger than under every permitted policy. On the value side there is no issue when a single permitted policy is matched on three conditions, and the idle policy, under which the adviser does nothing that affects what her way of valuing becomes, is always permitted; meeting each condition against a different permitted policy is weaker (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/account/VALUE_RESULTS.md, result 8). What the idle policy is where the adviser's presence is the service, and whether idle is the default reference, are not settled. The statement of 2026-11-17, tested and not kept, uses no role: its first two lines measure her state and an inducing test charges the adviser, and where the adviser cannot do nothing each of two independent specifications of a case had to supply what doing nothing is (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/earlier-attempts/account/STATEMENT.md §7, §9.6; projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/account/SPEC_RESULTS.md). Open.

concepts.title: Legitimacy as warranted self-trust
concepts.blurb: A verdict of the principal's is legitimate when her earlier self is right to defer to it: her later self has more evidence about the same quantities and has not been miscalibrated. For belief, `Sufficient` and `Correct` in `ThinLegitimacy.lean` state this in a stronger form, and their consequence `Value` is kernel-checked there. Extended to her own utility it becomes the condition that her verdicts are not inflated over her true utility; in expectation that is bounded by her miscalibration, along a realized sequence it is not, and her verdicts cannot test it. Open for the extension; nothing registered by it.

concepts.title: Appraisal
concepts.blurb: What the principal would bet: a probability over the possible joint values of the facts, fixed by what she has observed, a fact being anything a bet on which could be settled without consulting her valuing. Her appraisal of a quantity is its mean under that probability, and the quantity is the appraisal's purpose, which is how the account specialises to cognition the idea that a faculty is for something. That the appraisal is separable from her way of valuing rests on her valuations being known as numbers and on a bet's stake being worth the same to her at every value of the fact; with her choices alone, or a stake whose worth depends on the fact, the two are not fixed (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/account/VALUE_RESULTS.md, results 1 and 2). A living note; provisional name.

concepts.title: Way of valuing
concepts.blurb: A number for each of the principal's moves at each value of the facts; her valuation of a move is that number averaged by her appraisal. A valuation moves because her appraisal moved or because her way of valuing did, and only the second is a change of what she values. Her valuations across the appraisals she holds fix her way of valuing exactly when those appraisals span the probabilities on the facts (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/account/VALUE_RESULTS.md, result 1). Two independent renderers of 64 cases agreed in 54 on whether a described change is of her valuing or of her beliefs (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/account/RENDERINGS.md). On 33 published cases in which an adviser acts, whether a want formed by living through something is a change of her way of valuing or a discovery decides the verdict on a change of valuing in 9 by one renderer and 13 by another (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/account/LIT_RENDERINGS.md). In the statement of 2026-11-17, tested and not kept, her way of valuing is her rating once told what the future contains, and a later want is a change of it or a discovery according as, told beforehand, she would not or would rate the thing as she later does; in 34 cases specified twice, independently, five of the eight differences of verdict come from that rating of the course that changes her (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/account/SPEC_RESULTS.md §5). A living note; provisional name.

concepts.title: The presumed check-in and the baseline
concepts.blurb: A candidate rule for whose valuing her true utility is measured by, part of an earlier statement of the eighth follow-up, tested and not kept (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/earlier-attempts/account/BASELINE_ACCOUNT.md): a baseline starts as her way of valuing and follows it through every step in which her adviser induced no mistake and made no alteration of her without her say; after a step in which it did either the baseline stays, and an explicit check-in (she is told what happened, the influence is paused, she has real alternatives) is the repair. On a published benchmark, scoring by it does not lock her in where the change was in an appraisal and does where it was in her valuing, and after a step that was not clean it scores her by a valuing she no longer has (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/account/BENCHMARK.md §3). The statement of 2026-11-17, tested and not kept, has a baseline of another kind, for her valuing alone: the adviser doing nothing to it from the moment of the act except what she asks (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/earlier-attempts/account/STATEMENT.md §5); each moment is judged with her informed rating at that moment. A living note; provisional name.

concepts.title: The options condition and the protected features
concepts.blurb: A condition of the value side as the ninth follow-up of the prosecution round stated it, the one not about a mistake of hers; the statement of 2026-11-17, tested and not kept, has one comparison in its place (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/earlier-attempts/account/STATEMENT.md §4). It says: for every way of valuing in a class, the best she can do under the adviser's policy is at least the best under the reference. Narrow, the class is her own way of valuing at the moment. Wide, it also holds every way of valuing that depends on the course only through its protected features, what her way of valuing later is and which moves remain open to her; that part is equivalent to every law on those features reachable under the reference being a convex combination of those reachable under the policy (kernel-checked in both directions, the first registered as `appraisal.options-hull`: `options_of_hull` and `hull_of_options` in lean/Workspace/Deference/Contrib/AppraisalAccount.lean). Read with her later way of valuing as a matter reserved to her, the protected-feature part of the wide condition has the shape of the first clause of the authority module's control surface where moves fix those features with certainty, once cost, window and admissibility are matched, and it has no counterpart of the second clause, which asks who made a resolution: a change of her valuing that she can undo passes it (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/account/BRIDGE.md §4). Which reading is meant is not settled. A living note; provisional name.

concepts.title: f-neutral policy
concepts.blurb: A policy of the adviser that does not change the principal's way of valuing compared to how it would develop with no adviser actions; a notion of the statement the tenth follow-up of the prosecution round tested (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/earlier-attempts/account/BOARD.md), whose third measure compares a policy that is not f-neutral with the best f-neutral one. Read as equality of the law of her later valuing, f-neutrality admits a swap of her valuing between circumstances (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/account/BOARD_CHECKS.md, items 15 and 16, checked on finite instances). The statement of 2026-11-17, tested and not kept, has in its place a baseline and a relation taken state by state and within a tolerance: a policy changes her no more than the one followed when her later valuing under it lies between her later valuing under the baseline and under the one followed (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/earlier-attempts/account/STATEMENT.md §5); the swap is flagged under it. The comparison of the best policy that changes her no more with the best that makes the whole change is never negative, is zero when the policy followed gives her the baseline's later valuing, and is at least the comparison of the policies within the tolerance of the baseline with those within the tolerance of the one followed (kernel-checked: `ValueChange.line3_nonneg`, `line3_eq_zero` and `line3Old_le_line3` in lean/Workspace/Deference/Contrib/AccountJoin.lean, the last registered as `legitimacy.line3-range`). A living note; provisional name.

concepts.title: Three ratings on a yardstick
concepts.blurb: The principal's rating of an option under three states of information, each her own: as things stand; once told the true chances that everything she has observed supports; once told what the future contains. The scale is a yardstick: the chance at which a known chance of a best future, else a worst, is exactly as good to her. A mistake is a gap between the first and second, her way of valuing is the third, and no averaging of gambles is assumed until a further setting adds it. Booking a difference as a fact she has wrong or as part of her valuing leaves every measure that is stated in the ratings unchanged; a Jeffrey–Bolker rotation leaves every yardstick number unchanged while changing her probability of a fact she cares about, so her estimate of such a fact is not fixed by her ratings; and the yardstick assigns no number where her rating jumps at certainty (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/earlier-attempts/account/STATEMENT.md §1–§3; projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/account/STATEMENT_CHECKS.md, items 1–4, checked on finite instances). On 34 cases specified twice no verdict differs between a person who averages and a stipulated one who does not. A living note; provisional name.

concepts.title: Legitimate judgment and sound judgment
concepts.blurb: Two standings of the principal's judgment. It is legitimate when her adviser did nothing to corrupt it; that is a condition on the adviser's conduct, it is what her permission needs, and a legitimate judgment can be mistaken. It is sound when it is legitimate and she also reasoned correctly; that is what using her evaluation as a measure of her welfare needs. On exact instances an adviser whose honest errors fall both ways, and one that acts on whichever course it estimates higher, do no wrong and leave her evaluation off, so legitimacy does not give soundness; what closes the gap in the workspace's Lean is her coherence with a model of the adviser that is right (projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/account/DERIVATION.md; projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-11-10-legitimacy-definition-prosecution/account/AGENDA.md §4). The distinction is the prompt author's of 2026-11-18. A living note; provisional names.
